resolved_title: Calderdale Excellence Partnership: IPEELL. Evaluation report and executive summary (Education Endowment Foundation, November 2018)
notes: recoded after re-retrieval 2026-09-18: first page names Torgerson, Ainsworth, Bell, Elliott, Fountain, Gascoine, Hewitt, Kasim, Kokotsaki, and Torgerson (EEF, November 2018), the IPEELL effectiveness trial whose summary table gives Kraft's n 2,465 (one-year trial) and 2,196 (two-year trial). Eighty-four primary schools in Leeds and Lincolnshire were randomized 1:1; all Year 5 and Year 6 pupils in participating schools were eligible with parental opt-out (PDF p. 15), and there were no teacher criteria. Coded targeted_low at the school level by tie-breaker 1 because recruitment targeted schools on both low KS2 achievement and FSM share (recruited schools had 33.4 percent FSM against 14.5 nationally). Confidence medium because the only hard school criterion excluded Ofsted category four schools and the need-based targeting was a recruitment preference, so a reviewer could read the sample as universal.

Kraft's n 451 matches. Eighty-five percent low income, 46 percent Hispanic, 15 percent with a disability, but selection was on the score.
